summary: Registers the text/troff media subtype for content that mixes text with formatting directives, as used by the troff family of programs. It also describes how to convey the processing steps needed to produce formatted output. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Troff files are plain text sprinkled with formatting commands. This memo gives them an official label so programs know what they are.

questions: what is the troff mime type
what is a preprocessor in formatting
subtitle: An official label for documents that mix text with formatting commands.

tldr.problem: The troff family of text formatting programs mixes readable text with formatting directives, but internet systems had no standard way to label or identify such content when transmitted over the network.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4263 registers a MIME media type called text/troff, allowing senders to mark content with that type. The registration includes optional parameters to convey processing steps, required resources, and software versions needed.
tldr.outcome: Programs can now recognize troff source files and know they may need to be processed through formatters, preprocessors, and postprocessors before display. The media type remains informational guidance for registration.

today: RFC 4263 is an informational registration of the text/troff media type and has not been obsoleted or updated. The troff family of programs remains in use, particularly for formatting Unix manual pages and technical documentation, though its use has declined from its peak in the late 20th century.

sections.title: What is Troff
sections.content:
Troff is a family of text formatting programs that has existed since the early 1970s. The name is generic, though it also refers to a specific program lineage. Related programs include nroff, which formats text for character-based output (like terminal display), and earlier programs like roff and runoff.

The core idea is simple: text content is mixed with formatting directives. These directives control things like fonts, spacing, and layout. This approach has several benefits: readers can understand the text by ignoring the directives, and the same content can be repurposed for different output media by changing the directives. Troff has been used to produce everything from short memoranda to full books, including tables, diagrams, and mathematical content.
sections.eli5: Troff is like writing a document in Word, but instead of clicking buttons to make text bold or change fonts, you type special codes into the text itself.

sections.title: The Troff Ecosystem
sections.content:
Troff is not just a single tool but an ecosystem. Preprocessors transform text descriptions into troff directives. For example, the tbl preprocessor converts table descriptions into formatting commands, eqn formats mathematical equations, pic handles line drawings, and grap creates data charts. All these preprocessors produce output compatible with the troff formatter.

Macro packages extend troff's capabilities by providing sets of common formatting tools. Packages like ms, me, and man (used for Unix manual pages) simplify document creation. Postprocessors convert the formatter's output into device-specific formats. This ecosystem made troff flexible enough to remain in use for decades, including to write RFC documents themselves.
sections.eli5: Troff is really a whole system: programs that help you write charts and math, packages that provide templates, and programs that convert troff to other formats like PDF.

sections.title: Media Type Registration
sections.content:
RFC 4263 registers the MIME media type text/troff. This type has no required parameters, but includes optional ones to convey additional information about how the content should be processed. The charset parameter specifies the character encoding, with US-ASCII as the default for traditional troff content. Some modern implementations support Unicode input, though this may cause interoperability issues.

The process parameter is human-readable text describing the processing pipeline: which preprocessors to use, in what order, what formatter arguments to pass, and which postprocessors to apply. The resources parameter lists additional files or programs needed for formatting. The versions parameter indicates specific versions of tools required, helping ensure consistent output.
sections.eli5: The media type registration is like a package label that says 'this is troff content.' It can also include notes about what programs should open it and what options they need.

sections.title: Encoding and Transport
sections.content:
Troff content consists largely of printable ASCII characters, so 7bit encoding is adequate for traditional content. However, some lines may begin or end with whitespace, and mail systems can discard or mangle that whitespace. For safer transport, 7bit encoding with CRLF line endings is recommended as the canonical form.

Content with Unicode characters represented in UTF-8 may use 8bit encoding where transport allows. When Unicode characters are used extensively or line lengths exceed limits, binary encoding may be necessary. Regardless of encoding, line endings must be normalized to CRLF when transferring between systems using MIME protocols.
sections.eli5: Troff files are mostly plain text. They travel safely on the internet using basic text encoding, but sometimes special steps are needed if they have fancy characters.

sections.title: Security Risks in Troff Processing
sections.content:
Troff includes directives that can execute arbitrary external programs: .sy (system execute) and .pi (pipe input). Other directives can read external files or devices: .so (source file), .nx (next file), and .cf (file input). Some implementations provide a safe mode that disables these features. Additionally, formatters and preprocessors are programmable, and it is possible to write input that specifies infinite loops, causing denial of service.

Processing troff content from untrusted sources is dangerous. Users should be vigilant about the potential for damage. Processing should not be invoked automatically without user confirmation, and suggested command lines should be carefully scrutinized for social engineering attempts. Comments in troff source are readable in the document but not formatted, so they may leak sensitive information. Implementations must not presume that safe modes are available or active.
sections.eli5: Troff files can contain commands that run programs or read files, so opening a troff file from someone you do not trust could be risky. Like any powerful tool, it needs careful use.

sections.title: Portability Challenges
sections.content:
Troff content may not produce consistent output across different systems. Newer formatters, macro packages, and preprocessors include extensions not available in older implementations. Using such extensions limits the ability to generate the same output elsewhere. Macro packages themselves are often trademarks or copyrighted, leading to multiple independent implementations with subtle differences.

Different preprocessors and postprocessors may produce different results, even when implementing the same feature. For example, the pic preprocessor varies: some versions support fill color while others do not; those that do differ on whether 0.0 or 1.0 represents a solid fill. Devices have varying capabilities: some support only grayscale, others support color. A document designed for sophisticated formatting may not be representable on simpler media, though approximations are often possible.
sections.eli5: Troff documents might look different depending on what version of troff and what helpers you have on your computer. Old and new versions might disagree about how to display things.
